findings.summary: The stations-in-view live region lives inside the settings panel, which is hidden until opened, so pan, zoom, and load counts are not announced, and opening the panel does not read the count already written.
findings.fix:
Move the status node outside #map-settings-panel so it is never under hidden. Keep
in the first paint. In loadStations set textContent to "Loading stations in view" before fetch, then to "N stations in view" or "No stations in view". Call that again from openSettings.
findings.evidence: <aside id="map-settings-panel" hidden> wraps data-map-target="stationListStatus" role="status". openSettings removes hidden and does not update the status text.

findings.summary: A failed map refresh is written to the search status region inside the mobile search panel, which is hidden and display:none on desktop, so the error is not announced.
findings.fix: Announce the failure on a polite region that is not inside .map-mobile-search. Example: viewStatusTarget.textContent = "Couldn't refresh stations in view." Leave data-map-target="status" for search counts only. That node stays under hidden until search opens, and .map-mobile-search is md:hidden.
findings.evidence: this.statusTarget.textContent = "Couldn't refresh stations in view." Parent is .map-mobile-search[hidden] with Tailwind md:hidden (display:none from 768px).

findings.summary: Choosing Use my location on the map can take up to 10 seconds and then recenters the map without a polite announcement of the wait or the success.
findings.fix: On a polite region that exists on load, set textContent to "Finding your location" before getCurrentPosition and "Map centered on your location" in the success callback. Keep permission, timeout, and unsupported errors in the dialog, which already moves focus to OK.
findings.evidence: navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(..., { enableHighAccuracy: true, timeout: 10000 }) sets the view and adds a marker with no status text and no aria-busy.

findings.summary: Choosing Use my location on the home page can take up to 20 seconds and only toggles aria-busy, so screen reader users get no waiting announcement.
findings.fix: Call this.announce("Finding the nearest station") at the start of locate, using the existing role="status" target. Clear it when navigation starts. Keep aria-busy on the button, but do not treat it as the status message. Errors already open the dialog and move focus.
findings.evidence: setLocateBusy only sets disabled and aria-busy. getCurrentPosition timeout is 20000. The status target is not updated.

findings.summary: The state directory and flood-alert search write a new polite result count on every keystroke, so screen readers queue a station count for each character.
findings.fix:
Debounce the status text about 500ms after input. Update it immediately for checkbox changes. Do not write the count from connect(). Keep the empty
and set textContent to "N stations shown" or "No stations match these filters."
findings.evidence: data-action="input->state-directory#filter" and filter() assigns statusTarget.textContent with no timer. connect() calls filter().

findings.summary: Contact and subscription success and error messages are rendered already filled in the first HTML response, so their status and alert roles are not announced after submit.
findings.fix: Do not ship role="status" or role="alert" already filled. Focus the flash on load with tabindex="-1" and autofocus, or copy it into an empty live region from the first paint after load. On field errors, focus the first [aria-invalid="true"] control so aria-describedby is read. Use role="status" for the success notice and role="alert" only for the error.
findings.evidence: Flashes use role=status and role=alert only inside <% if flash %>. #contact-turnstile-error is role=alert in that same response. Forms set data-turbo=false. No autofocus.

passed: Home station search announces polite result counts from a status region present before the fetch, using textContent, after a 200ms debounce so each keystroke is not announced.
Map station search uses that same polite count announcement once the mobile search panel is open.
Search suggestion lists are listboxes updated with innerHTML, not live regions, so the full list is not re-read.
Directory checkbox and flood-stage changes write one polite station count per change.
No aria-live=assertive is used for search, filter, or map updates. role=alert is reserved for form errors.
Geolocation errors open a dialog, move focus to OK, and expose the message as the dialog description.
Home and directory status regions use .sr-only clipping, not display:none or visibility:hidden.
Layer filter changes announce a station count when the map settings panel is already open.
About, privacy, terms, disclosures, and acceptable use do not change content after load.
FAQ answers are disclosures with aria-expanded, not live regions.
No toast, snackbar, or auto-dismiss banner exists, so none disappear before they can be read.
Contact field errors are tied to inputs with aria-invalid and aria-describedby.
notes: Map station fetch and both station searches have no timeout and no loading text. Source does not prove those requests last longer than about two seconds. Geolocation timeouts do: 10 seconds on the map and 20 seconds on the home page.

state-directory filter() runs from connect() and writes the initial count during page load. Whether assistive technologies speak that, or drop it for the page-load announcement, cannot be proven from source.
Contact and subscription forms return a full document (data-turbo=false). The on-load alert finding follows the ARIA alert pattern; a screen reader was not run.
FAQ category buttons swap hidden sections and set aria-current, with no status region. Scored as navigation, not as a result count.
Hiding a focused station card can move keyboard focus. Not scored; the result count is still written to the status region.
app/javascript/map.js only registers the map controllers. app/javascript/lib/geolocation_errors.js only returns dialog title and body copy.

Flood-alert and state-directory lists are server-rendered and do not poll. Turnstile errors inside the Cloudflare iframe were not reviewed. The manage-link email field uses native required validation, which was not executed.

Search responses that are not OK return without a visible error or status text in station_search_controller.js and map_controller.js fetchSearchResults. Nothing on screen changes, so this was not scored as a missed announcement.
No toast library was assumed. Source for the scoped public pages has no toast, snackbar, or dismiss timer.
